5.6

Reference

mixture.

This International Standard specifies a method for the detection of linear condensed phosphates in meat and meat products by thin layer chromatographic separation.

Dissolve in 109 ml of water. 200 mg of sodium dihydrogen phosphate monohydrate (NaH*P04.HzO), 300 mg of tetrasodium (Na4P207.10H20), diphosphate decahydrate

2

Field of application

Since polyphosphates are gradually hydrolyzed by enzymes present in the meat or meat product and during heat treatment of the meat or meat product, this International Standard only applies to the detection of added polyphosphates that are still present in the sample at the time of investigation.

200 mg of pentasodium triphosphate (NasPsOlel, and

200 mg of sodium hexametaphosphate (NaPOs),[x > 101. The reference mixture is stable at 4 "C for at least 4 weeks.

IS0 3100, Meet and meat products -

Mix 146 ml of isopropyl alcohol, 40 ml of a 135 g/l solution of trichloroacetic~acid, and 0,6 ml of ammonium hydroxide, ~2~ = 0.90 g/ml; about 25 % (m/m) solution. Keep the solvent in a tightly closed bottle.

4

Principle

Extraction of the meat or meat product -with trichlornacetic acid. Clearing of the serum~obtained with ethanol/diethyl ether mixture. Separation of the phosphates by thin layer chromatography and detection of polyphosphates by spraying with reagents for colour development.

5.8 , Spray reagent I. Mix equal volumes of a 75 g/l solution of ammonium molvbdate tetrahydrate [(NH4)sMo7024.4H201 and concentrated nitric acid (em = 1.40 g/ml) and dissolve 10 g of tartaric acid in 190 ml of this mixture. Prepare the reagent on the day of use.

5

Reagents

All reagents shall be of recognized analytical quality. Distilled water or water of at least equivalent purity shall be used. :' Warning - All appropriate safety precautions shall be observed when carrying out the procedures specified in this International Standard. 5.1 5.2 5.3 5.4 5.5 Trichloroacetic Diethyl ether. Ethanol, 95 % ( V/ v). Cellulose powder, Soluble starch. `3 for thin, layer chromatography. acid.

5.9

Spray reagent II.

#

Dissolve 0,5 g of 1-amino-2-naphthol-4-sulphonic acid in a mixture of 195 ml of a 150 g/l solution of sodium disulphite (sodium metabisulphite;Na2S205) and 5 ml of a 200 g/l solution of sodium sulphite (Na2S03). Dissolve 40 g of sodium acetate trihydrate (Na00CCH3.3H20) in this mixture. Store the reagent in a tightly closed brown bottle in the refrigerator. Discard the solution after 1 week.

8.2

~Preparation of the test sample

Spreading device, for preparing layers of 0,25 mm thickness. ~If such a device is not available, ready-to-use thinlayer plates with layer thicknesses of 0,25 mm can be used provided that starch is used as the binder. Plates containing gypsum (calcium sulphate) are not suitable.

Homogenize the sample by passing it at least twice through the meat mincer (6.5) and by mixing. Keep it in a completely filled, air-tight, closed container and store it, if necessary, fin a refrigerator. Analyse the sample as soon as possible, but in any case within.5 h.

6.3 6.4 6.6

Laboratory Desiccator.

mixer.

8.3

Preparation

of serum

Mechanical meat mincer, laboratory size, fitted with a plate with holes of diameter not exceeding 4 mm. Fluted filter paper, of diameter 15 cm. with micrometer

8.3.1 Macerate 50 g of the test sample (8.2) with 15 ml of water at 40 to 60 T in a beaker by means of a spatula or a flattened stirring rod until a homogeneous mass is obtained, but taking no more than 5 min. 8.32 Add 10 g of the trichloroacetic acid (5.1) and again mix thoroughly. 8.3.3 Immediately place in a refrigerator for 1 h and then collect the separated serum by decanting through the fluted filter paper (6.6). 8.3.4 If the filtrate is turbid, shake once with an equal volume of the diethyl ether (5.2). Remove the ether layer with a small pipette and add an equal volume of the ethanol (5.3) to the aqueous phase. Shake for 1 min. Allow the mixture to stand for a few minutes and filter through a fluted filter paper (6.6).

Sample

8.4.1 Pour developing solvent 15.7) into the developing tank (6.8) to a depth ~of5 to 10 mm and close the tank with its lid. Allow to stand for at least 30 min at ambient temperature, protected from sunlight and draughts. 8.4.2 Apply 3 pl of the serum, or 6 pl if the clearing procedure of 8.3.4 was carried out, to the cellulose layer (8.1) on a pencil line drawn at about 2 cm from the bottom. Keep the spots small by applying 1 j.11 at a time. Use a warm air stream from the hair-dryer (6.91 for drying.

7.1 Proceed from a laboratory sample of at least 200 g. See IS0 3100. 7.2 Prepare the test sample on the day of its receipt in the laboratory.

8
8.1

Procedure
Preparation of thin-layer plates

NOTE - Hot air shouldbe avoidedbecauseof the dangerof hydrolysis of phosphates.

Dissolve 0.3 g of starch (5.5) in 90 ml of boiling water. Cool, add 15 g of cellulose powder (5.4) and homogenize in the laboratory mixer (6.3) for 1 min. Apply this slurry onto glass plates (6.1) with the spreading device (6.2) adjusted to obtain a layer of 0.25 mm. Air-dry the plates undisturbed for 60 min at room temperature and heat them finally for 10 min at 100 OC. Store the plates in the desiccator (6.41. Alternatively, ready-to-use thin-layer plates may be used (see 6.2). 4

8.4.3 In the same way, apply 3 pl of the reference mixture (5.6) to the plate at a distance of 1 to 15 cm from the sample spot, but at exactly the same distance from the bottom. 8.4.4 Remove the lid from the tank and quickly but carefully place the cellulose plate in the tank. Replace the lid immediately. Develop the plate at ambient temperature, protected from sunlight and draughts. 8.4.5 Continue the development until the solvent front has ascended approximately 10 cm from the pencil line. Remove the plate from the tank and dry for 10 min in the oven (6.11) controlled at 60 OC, or alternatively, for 30 min at ambient temperature, or in a stream of cold air.

8.5 8.5.1

Detection

of phosphates

The RF values of the phosphates in the reference mixture are : orthophosphate diphosphate (pyrophosphate) from 080 to 090 from 0.50 to 060 from 0,25 to 0,35 0.0

Place the plate vertically under a fume hood and spray the plate lightly but uniformly with spray reagent I (5.8). Yellow spots appear immediately.

triphosphate 8.5.2 Dry the plate in a stream of warm air from the hair dryer (6.9). Subsequently heat in an oven for at least 1 h at 100 OCto remove the last traces of nitric acid. Remove the plate from the oven and verify the absence of the pungent smell of nitric acid. 8.6.3 Allow the plate to cool to room temperature and then replace it under the fume hood. Spray the plate lightly but uniformly with spray reagent II (5.9). Blue spots appear immediately.
NOTE - Spraying with reagent II is not an absolute nacessity. However, the intense blue spots produced by this reagent `mproye the detection considerably.

hexcrmetapolyphosphate (Graham's salt)

Generally the RF values of the polyphosphates in extracts of meat and meat products are somewhat lower.
NOTE Corrections for the differences in RF values of the phosphates in the sample extract and in the reference mixture can be obtained by placing an extract of the fresh meat sample on the same plate. As fresh meat only contains monophosphates, the percentage correction can be obtained by comparison of the migration distances of this standard spot with the corresponding spot from the reference mixture.

9

10
Interpretation

Test report

The test report shall show the method Compare mixture. the migration distances of `he phosphate spots from the sample with those of the pnosphates from the reference

used and the results obtained. It shall also mention all operating conditions not specified in this International Standard or regarded as optional, as well as any circumstances that may have influenced the results. The &port shall include all details necessary for complete identification of the sample.

An orthophosphate spot is~always present. If the sample contained condensed phosphates, a diphosphate spot and/or spots of more highly polymerized phosphates are visible.
